Interface OidcGrant

public interface OidcGrant
Authorization state bound to the end user's provider session.

An authorization endpoint fills one of these in twice. The validated authorization request goes in first — getClientId(), getRedirectUri(), getScope(), getResource(), getState(), getNonce(), and getCodeChallenge() — so the request survives the round trip to the identity provider without riding on a return URI that provider would see. Once a principal is established the rest is filled in and the user agent gets an authorization code naming it.

A set getClientId() is what marks a session as carrying a request; once a code is issued the detail is cleared, so the session no longer resumes. A session handler proxies this interface over encrypted session storage, so none of these values reach the user agent — only the session cookie does.

The completed grant is not what the authorization code names. It is signed, encrypted, and handed to the token endpoint through GrantStore, which the code is the decryption key for, so this interface is also the claim the grant token carries. A token endpoint redeems that token, checking getClientId(), getRedirectUri(), and getCodeChallenge() before issuing an ID token.

    • getRequestedAuthorizationDetails

      Iterable<? extends edu.iu.jwt.IuAuthorizationDetails> getRequestedAuthorizationDetails()
      Gets the authorization details the client asked for, as its transport parsed them.

      Recorded before the end user is known, since a client states what it wants without waiting to find out who is asking. What was actually granted is getReleasedAuthorizationDetails(), and the two are kept apart so a grant says both what was sought and what came of it.

      Returns:
      requested authorization details; null if the request asked for none
      See Also:
      • RFC 9396: OAuth 2.0 Rich Authorization Requests

    • setRequestedAuthorizationDetails

      void setRequestedAuthorizationDetails(Iterable<? extends edu.iu.jwt.IuAuthorizationDetails> requestedAuthorizationDetails)
      Sets the authorization details the client asked for.
      Parameters:
      requestedAuthorizationDetails - requested authorization details

    • getReleasedAuthorizationDetails

      Iterable<? extends edu.iu.jwt.IuAuthorizationDetails> getReleasedAuthorizationDetails()
      Gets the authorization details released to the end user.

      Decided once, after the end user is authenticated and before an authorization code is issued, so a client redeeming this grant — directly, or through a refresh token descending from it — reads a decision already made rather than one remade on every redemption. This is what a token endpoint publishes as the granted authorization_details.

      Returns:
      released authorization details; null if none were released
      See Also:
      • IuOidcAuthorizationDetailsSource

      Parameters:

    • getResource

      String[] getResource()
      Gets the resource parameter values named when the code was issued.

      Recorded so a token endpoint redeeming this grant — directly, or through a refresh token descending from it — can restrict the audience it addresses a token to at most what was named here, rather than trusting whatever resource the redemption request happens to carry. A request naming a subset narrows the audience further; one naming something not here is refused.

      Returns:
      resource URIs requested; null or empty if the request named none, which leaves the audience bounded by granted scope alone
